items.name: Louvre Museum
items.description: The Mona Lisa, the Venus de Milo and about 30,000 other things. Book the first slot and start at the Denon wing.

items.name: Eiffel Tower summit
items.description: Lift to the second floor, then the summit lift for the view down the Champ de Mars.

items.name: Seine dinner cruise
items.description: Three courses while Notre-Dame, the Louvre and the Musée d'Orsay slide past the window.

items.name: Le Marais food walking tour
items.description: Falafel on Rue des Rosiers, fromagerie stops, and a bakery that has been running since 1900.

items.name: Montmartre and Sacré-Cœur
items.description: Climb to the basilica for the free city view, then wander the painters' square at Place du Tertre.

items.name: Moulin Rouge show
items.description: The original Belle Époque cabaret. Feathers, champagne and a very long-running can-can.

items.name: Colosseum and Roman Forum
items.description: One ticket covers the arena, the Forum and Palatine Hill. Go early — the shade runs out by ten.

items.name: Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel
items.description: Four kilometres of galleries ending under Michelangelo's ceiling. Timed entry is essential.

items.name: Trastevere food tour
items.description: Supplì, carbonara and a family-run gelateria across the river from the tourist crush.

items.name: Pantheon and Piazza Navona walk
items.description: The best-preserved Roman building anywhere, then Bernini's fountains two streets away.

items.name: Pasta-making class in Monti
items.description: Hand-roll cacio e pepe and tonnarelli, then eat what you made with a glass of Frascati.

items.name: Borghese Gallery
items.description: Bernini's Apollo and Daphne in a villa set in gardens. Strict two-hour entry slots.

items.name: Sagrada Família
items.description: Gaudí's unfinished basilica. Afternoon light through the west windows is the reason to time it right.

items.name: Park Güell
items.description: Mosaic terraces above the city. The monumental zone is ticketed; the surrounding park is free.

items.name: La Boqueria and Gothic Quarter tapas crawl
items.description: Market pintxos, jamón ibérico and vermouth through the medieval lanes.

items.name: Picasso Museum
items.description: His early Barcelona years, in five linked medieval palaces on Carrer Montcada.

items.name: Barceloneta beach afternoon
items.description: City beach with a boardwalk of chiringuitos. Busy in August, perfect in May.

items.name: Flamenco at Palau de la Música
items.description: Modernista concert hall with stained glass overhead and serious guitar work on stage.

items.name: Rijksmuseum
items.description: Vermeer, Rembrandt's Night Watch, and a Dutch Golden Age collection worth the whole morning.

items.name: Anne Frank House
items.description: The secret annexe behind the bookcase. Tickets release six weeks ahead and sell out same-day.

items.name: Canal cruise at dusk
items.description: The seventeenth-century ring canals with the bridge lights coming on.

items.name: Jordaan cheese and stroopwafel tasting
items.description: Aged Gouda, bitterballen and a warm stroopwafel pressed in front of you.

items.name: Vondelpark bike ride
items.description: Rent a city bike and ride the park loop — the least stressful cycling in the city.

items.name: Albert Cuyp Market
items.description: Two hundred stalls of flowers, fabric and street food in De Pijp.

items.name: Prague Castle and St Vitus Cathedral
items.description: The largest ancient castle complex in the world, with Golden Lane inside the walls.

items.name: Charles Bridge at sunrise
items.description: Thirty baroque statues and no crowds — but only before about seven.

items.name: Old Town Square and the Astronomical Clock
items.description: The apostles parade on the hour. Arrive five minutes early for a spot.

items.name: Czech beer hall tour
items.description: Tank Pilsner in the old halls, plus a stop at a microbrewery the tour groups miss.

items.name: Vltava river lunch cruise
items.description: Castle views from the water with a buffet of Czech classics.

items.name: Vyšehrad fortress and vineyards
items.description: The quiet fort on the other hill, with a cemetery of Czech composers and a view down the river.

items.name: Tram 28 through Alfama
items.description: The old yellow tram grinding up through the oldest quarter. Board at Martim Moniz for a seat.

items.name: Belém Tower and Jerónimos Monastery
items.description: Manueline stonework from the age of exploration, both a short walk apart.

items.name: Pastéis de Belém tasting
items.description: The original custard tarts, still made to the 1837 recipe. Eat them warm with cinnamon.

items.name: Fado dinner in Bairro Alto
items.description: Portuguese blues in a small room where the lights go down between songs.

items.name: Sintra day trip
items.description: Pena Palace and the Quinta da Regaleira initiation well, forty minutes by train.

items.name: LX Factory browsing
items.description: Old industrial complex turned bookshops, design studios and rooftop bars under the bridge.

items.name: Oia sunset from the castle ruins
items.description: The famous one. Claim a spot on the wall ninety minutes early or watch from a Fira terrace instead.

items.name: Catamaran caldera cruise
items.description: Hot springs, the Red and White beaches, and a barbecue on deck as the sun drops.

items.name: Assyrtiko wine tasting at Santo Wines
items.description: Volcanic-soil whites tasted on a terrace hanging straight over the caldera.

items.name: Akrotiri archaeological site
items.description: A Bronze Age town buried by the eruption and preserved under ash — the Aegean Pompeii.

items.name: Red Beach swim
items.description: Iron-red cliffs dropping into clear water. Water shoes help on the pebbles.

items.name: Fira to Oia cliff walk
items.description: Ten kilometres along the caldera rim through Imerovigli. Start early; there is no shade.

items.name: Blue Lagoon
items.description: Geothermal silica water at 38°C in a lava field. Pre-booked slots only.

items.name: Golden Circle tour
items.description: Þingvellir rift valley, the Geysir field and Gullfoss waterfall in one loop.

items.name: Northern lights hunt
items.description: Chase clear sky away from the city lights. September to March, and never guaranteed.

items.name: Hallgrímskirkja tower
items.description: Lift to the top of the basalt-column church for the coloured rooftops and the bay.

items.name: Icelandic seafood tasting
items.description: Langoustine, arctic char and cured lamb — plus fermented shark if you insist.

items.name: Whale watching from the Old Harbour
items.description: Minke and humpback in Faxaflói bay. Dress for weather twenty degrees colder than shore.

items.name: Jungfraujoch railway
items.description: Cog railway to the highest station in Europe, 3,454m, through the Eiger itself.

items.name: Paragliding over Lake Thun
items.description: Tandem launch off Beatenberg with the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau on one side.

items.name: Harder Kulm funicular
items.description: Ten minutes up to a viewing platform on stilts above both lakes.

items.name: Lake Brienz boat cruise
items.description: Turquoise glacial water past Giessbach Falls on a steamer.

items.name: Swiss fondue dinner
items.description: Gruyère and Vacherin in a chalet, with kirsch and a basket of day-old bread.

items.name: Trümmelbach Falls
items.description: Ten glacier waterfalls inside the mountain, reached by a tunnel lift.

items.name: Senso-ji and Nakamise-dori
items.description: Tokyo's oldest temple, approached down a lane of snack and souvenir stalls.

items.name: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast
items.description: Tamagoyaki, uni and grilled scallops standing up, from about seven in the morning.

items.name: Shibuya Crossing and Hachiko
items.description: Three thousand people a light. Watch it from the Starbucks window, then walk it yourself.

items.name: TeamLab Planets
items.description: Barefoot digital art — you wade through knee-deep water full of projected koi.

items.name: Golden Gai bar hopping
items.description: Six alleys of bars seating six people each. Check for a cover charge before you sit.

items.name: Omoide Yokocho yakitori
items.description: Charcoal skewers and highballs under the tracks in Shinjuku's Memory Lane.

items.name: Fushimi Inari at sunrise
items.description: Ten thousand vermilion torii up the mountain. Before seven you will have them almost alone.

items.name: Arashiyama bamboo grove
items.description: The bamboo path, then Tenryu-ji's garden and the Togetsukyo bridge.

items.name: Kinkaku-ji Golden Pavilion
items.description: Gold leaf reflected in the mirror pond — the most photographed building in Japan.

items.name: Gion evening walk
items.description: Wooden machiya teahouses on Hanamikoji at dusk. Photographing geiko in the private lanes is banned.

items.name: Tea ceremony in Higashiyama
items.description: Whisk your own matcha in a tatami room after a lesson in the sequence.

items.name: Nishiki Market food crawl
items.description: Four hundred years of pickles, tofu doughnuts and skewered baby octopus down one covered street.

items.name: Tegallalang rice terraces
items.description: Stepped paddies north of Ubud. Small donations at each terrace gate.

items.name: Uluwatu Temple and Kecak fire dance
items.description: Clifftop temple 70m above the surf, with the chanting Ramayana performance at sunset.

items.name: Sunrise trek up Mount Batur
items.description: A 2am start for a two-hour climb, breakfast cooked in volcanic steam at the top.

items.name: Balinese cooking class in Ubud
items.description: Market shop, then base gede spice paste, sate lilit and black rice pudding.

items.name: Canggu surf lesson
items.description: Beginner beach break at Batu Bolong with board and rashguard included.

items.name: Spa afternoon in Seminyak
items.description: Two hours of Balinese massage, flower bath and ginger tea for the price of a cocktail at home.

items.name: Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew
items.description: The Emerald Buddha inside the royal compound. Covered shoulders and knees, no exceptions.

items.name: Wat Arun at sunset
items.description: Porcelain-encrusted spires across the Chao Phraya. Cross on the 4-baht ferry.

items.name: Chinatown street food crawl
items.description: Yaowarat after dark: crab curry, oyster omelette, mango sticky rice, on plastic stools.

items.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
items.description: Fifteen thousand stalls across 27 sections. Go at nine before the heat sets in.

items.name: Longtail boat through the klongs
items.description: The canals of Thonburi, where stilt houses and temple docks back onto the water.

items.name: Rooftop cocktails at Sky Bar
items.description: Open-air bar 63 floors up on Silom. Smart dress enforced at the lift.

items.name: Gardens by the Bay and the Supertree show
items.description: Cloud Forest dome and the free light show under the Supertrees at 7:45 and 8:45.

items.name: Hawker dinner at Maxwell Food Centre
items.description: Hainanese chicken rice, char kway teow and sugarcane juice for under fifteen dollars.

items.name: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark
items.description: The observation deck on the boat-shaped roof, 200m over the bay.

items.name: Singapore Zoo and Night Safari
items.description: Open-enclosure zoo by day, tram through nocturnal habitats after dark.

items.name: Kampong Glam and Haji Lane
items.description: Independent boutiques and murals in the shophouse lanes beside Sultan Mosque.

items.name: Singapore Sling at Raffles Long Bar
items.description: Where the drink was invented in 1915. Peanut shells still go on the floor.

items.name: Burj Khalifa At the Top
items.description: Levels 124 and 125 of the tallest building on earth. Sunset slots cost roughly double.

items.name: Desert safari with dune bashing
items.description: 4x4 over the red dunes, camel ride, then a barbecue camp under the stars.

items.name: Dubai Mall and the Fountain show
items.description: 1,200 shops, an aquarium wall, and fountains firing every half hour from six.

items.name: Old Dubai souks and abra crossing
items.description: Gold and spice souks either side of the Creek, linked by a 1-dirham wooden boat.

items.name: Dinner cruise on Dubai Marina
items.description: Dhow buffet with the Marina towers lit up on both banks.

items.name: Jumeirah Beach afternoon
items.description: Public white-sand beach looking straight at the Burj Al Arab.

items.name: Amber Fort
items.description: Hilltop fort above Maota Lake, with the mirror work of the Sheesh Mahal inside.

items.name: Hawa Mahal
items.description: The Palace of Winds — 953 windows built so royal women could watch the street unseen.

items.name: City Palace and Jantar Mantar
items.description: Working royal residence next to an eighteenth-century observatory of giant stone instruments.

items.name: Rajasthani thali at LMB
items.description: Dal baati churma, gatte ki sabzi and endless refills in Johari Bazaar.

items.name: Block-printing workshop in Sanganer
items.description: Carve, dye and print your own indigo cloth with a family that has done it for generations.

items.name: Johari Bazaar jewellery browsing
items.description: Kundan and meenakari work in the old gem quarter. Haggling is expected, not rude.

items.name: Palolem Beach day
items.description: Crescent bay in the south with calm water and beach shacks serving all day.

items.name: Old Goa churches
items.description: Basilica of Bom Jesus and Sé Cathedral — Portuguese baroque, and a UNESCO site.

items.name: Anjuna flea market
items.description: Wednesday market on the cliffs, running since the 1970s hippie years.

items.name: Spice plantation tour with lunch
items.description: Walk through cardamom and vanilla vines, then a banana-leaf Goan thali.

items.name: Dudhsagar Falls jeep safari
items.description: 310m of falls in the Western Ghats, reached by a rough jeep track through the forest.

items.name: Sunset cruise on the Mandovi
items.description: Live Konkani music and dancing on deck as the river turns orange.

items.name: Old Quarter walking tour
items.description: Thirty-six guild streets, each still named for the trade it once sold.

items.name: Bun cha lunch at Huong Lien
items.description: Grilled pork in fish sauce broth. Obama and Bourdain ate at the table upstairs.

items.name: Hoan Kiem Lake and Ngoc Son Temple
items.description: The red bridge to the island temple, best at six when the whole city exercises around it.

items.name: Thang Long water puppet show
items.description: A thousand-year-old art performed waist-deep behind a bamboo screen.

items.name: Egg coffee at Cafe Giang
items.description: Whipped yolk and condensed milk over strong coffee, invented here in 1946.

items.name: Ha Long Bay day cruise
items.description: Limestone karsts, a cave stop and kayaking. A long day trip, but the reason most people come.

items.name: Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island
items.description: Ferry from Battery Park. Crown tickets sell out months ahead; pedestal access does not.

items.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
items.description: Two million works. Pick three wings and accept you will not see the rest.

items.name: Broadway show
items.description: Same-day TKTS booth in Times Square discounts up to half off if you are flexible.

items.name: Katz's Delicatessen
items.description: Hand-carved pastrami on rye since 1888. Keep the ticket they hand you at the door.

items.name: High Line and Chelsea Market
items.description: Elevated park on a disused rail line, ending at a food hall in the old Nabisco factory.

items.name: Top of the Rock at sunset
items.description: Better than the Empire State, because the Empire State is in the view.

items.name: Golden Gate Bridge bike ride
items.description: Rent at Fisherman's Wharf, cross to Sausalito, take the ferry back.

items.name: Alcatraz Island tour
items.description: The cellhouse audio tour, narrated by former guards and inmates. Book weeks ahead.

items.name: Ferry Building Marketplace
items.description: Oysters, Cowgirl Creamery cheese and a farmers' market on Saturday mornings.

items.name: Cable car to Lombard Street
items.description: Powell-Hyde line up Russian Hill to the eight-hairpin block of Lombard.

items.name: Mission District taqueria crawl
items.description: Mission burritos on Valencia, plus the murals in Balmy Alley between stops.

items.name: Muir Woods redwoods
items.description: Thousand-year-old coast redwoods across the bridge. Parking reservations are mandatory.

items.name: Stanley Park seawall cycle
items.description: Ten kilometres of waterfront path around a 400-hectare forest inside the city.

items.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge
items.description: 137m across and 70m above the river, plus a cliff walk bolted to the granite.

items.name: Granville Island Public Market
items.description: Seafood, produce and bakeries under one roof, reached by a tiny rainbow ferry.

items.name: Grouse Mountain skyride
items.description: Gondola to 1,200m for the whole city, the bay and the Gulf Islands on a clear day.

items.name: Gastown and the steam clock
items.description: Cobbled original townsite, with a clock that whistles steam on the quarter hour.

items.name: Sunset kayak on False Creek
items.description: Flat water paddling with the downtown towers going gold behind you.

items.name: Teotihuacán pyramids
items.description: The Avenue of the Dead between the Sun and Moon pyramids, an hour outside the city.

items.name: Frida Kahlo Museum
items.description: La Casa Azul in Coyoacán, where she was born and died. Timed tickets online only.

items.name: Roma Norte taco tour
items.description: Al pastor off the trompo, suadero, and a mezcal stop between them.

items.name: Chapultepec Castle
items.description: The only royal castle in the Americas, on a hill in a park twice the size of Central Park.

items.name: Xochimilco trajinera boats
items.description: Painted flat-bottomed boats poled through Aztec-era canals, with mariachi for hire.

items.name: Lucha libre at Arena México
items.description: Masked wrestling on Friday nights. Buy the mask outside, wear it inside.

items.name: Christ the Redeemer
items.description: Cog train up through Tijuca forest to the 30m statue on Corcovado.

items.name: Sugarloaf Mountain cable car
items.description: Two stages to 396m, with the whole bay and Copacabana laid out below.

items.name: Ipanema Beach afternoon
items.description: Posto 9 for the people-watching, and the Arpoador rock for the sunset applause.

items.name: Feijoada lunch in Lapa
items.description: Black bean and pork stew with orange and farofa — traditionally a Saturday meal.

items.name: Samba night in Lapa
items.description: Live roda de samba under the arches. Friday is the night locals actually go.

items.name: Tijuca rainforest hike
items.description: The largest urban forest in the world, up to Pedra Bonita for the hang-glider view.

items.name: Machu Picchu day trip
items.description: Train to Aguas Calientes, bus up the switchbacks, timed circuit through the citadel.

items.name: Sacred Valley tour
items.description: Pisac terraces, the Ollantaytambo fortress and the salt pans at Maras.

items.name: Rainbow Mountain trek
items.description: Vinicunca at 5,200m. Acclimatise in Cusco for two days first or you will suffer.

items.name: San Pedro Market
items.description: Alpaca knitwear, forty kinds of potato, and juice stalls that will blend anything.

items.name: Peruvian cooking class
items.description: Ceviche, lomo saltado and a pisco sour you shake yourself.

items.name: Qorikancha and Cusco Cathedral
items.description: A Dominican convent built directly on Inca stonework that has outlasted every earthquake.

items.name: Tango show in San Telmo
items.description: Dinner and a live orchestra in a nineteenth-century hall, with a lesson beforehand.

items.name: Recoleta Cemetery
items.description: Six thousand marble mausoleums in city blocks, including Eva Perón's.

items.name: Parrilla steak dinner in Palermo
items.description: Bife de chorizo over wood coals with a Mendoza Malbec. Dinner starts at nine here.

items.name: La Boca and Caminito
items.description: Painted corrugated houses and street tango. Stay on the main streets and go by day.

items.name: San Telmo Sunday market
items.description: Antiques and buskers down thirteen blocks of Defensa, every Sunday.

items.name: Teatro Colón guided tour
items.description: One of the three best acoustics in the world, seen from the stage and the golden hall.

items.name: Table Mountain cableway
items.description: Rotating car to the flat top. Check the wind before you go — it closes often.

items.name: Cape Peninsula and Boulders penguins
items.description: Chapman's Peak drive, the Cape of Good Hope, and an African penguin colony on the way back.

items.name: Stellenbosch wine tasting
items.description: Three estates in the Cape Winelands, with Chenin Blanc and Pinotage on every list.

items.name: Robben Island tour
items.description: Ferry to the prison where Mandela spent eighteen years, guided by former political prisoners.

items.name: Bo-Kaap walk and Cape Malay cooking
items.description: The painted quarter on Signal Hill, then rolling samosas and cooking bobotie in a family kitchen.

items.name: Camps Bay sunset
items.description: White sand under the Twelve Apostles, with the sun dropping into the Atlantic.

items.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa after dark
items.description: The main square turns into a food market, storytellers and gnawa drummers at sunset.

items.name: Bahia Palace and the Saadian Tombs
items.description: Carved cedar ceilings and zellige tilework, plus a necropolis sealed up for two centuries.

items.name: Souk shopping in the medina
items.description: Lanterns, leather and argan oil. Start at a third of the asking price and stay friendly.

items.name: Traditional hammam and spa
items.description: Black soap, steam and a gommage scrub, followed by mint tea on a riad roof.

items.name: Moroccan tagine cooking class
items.description: Shop the spice souk with a dada, then cook lamb with preserved lemon over charcoal.

items.name: Agafay Desert sunset camel ride
items.description: Stony desert forty minutes out, with the Atlas range going pink behind the dunes.

items.name: Stone Town walking tour
items.description: Carved Zanzibari doors, the old slave market memorial and the House of Wonders.

items.name: Spice farm tour
items.description: Clove, nutmeg and cinnamon straight off the tree, with a fruit tasting to finish.

items.name: Prison Island and giant tortoises
items.description: Short dhow ride to Changuu, home to Aldabra tortoises over a century old.

items.name: Nungwi Beach day
items.description: The northern tip, where the tide barely moves the swimming and the water stays turquoise.

items.name: Forodhani night market
items.description: Grilled seafood skewers and Zanzibari pizza in the harbour gardens.

items.name: Sunset dhow cruise
items.description: Traditional lateen sail out of the old harbour as the call to prayer carries over the water.

items.name: Sydney Opera House tour
items.description: Inside the shells, including the concert hall and the story of how the roof was solved.

items.name: Bondi to Coogee coastal walk
items.description: Six kilometres of clifftop path past Tamarama, Bronte and the Waverley cemetery.

items.name: Harbour Bridge Climb
items.description: Up the arch to 134m, harnessed to the rail the whole way. Dawn climbs are the best value.

items.name: Taronga Zoo by ferry
items.description: Twelve-minute ferry from Circular Quay to a hillside zoo with the skyline behind the giraffes.

items.name: Sydney Fish Market lunch
items.description: Sydney rock oysters and barramundi at the largest fish market in the southern hemisphere.

items.name: Manly Beach ferry afternoon
items.description: The 30-minute ferry across the heads is the best-value harbour cruise in the city.

items.name: Kawarau Bridge bungy jump
items.description: The original commercial bungy, 43m over the river. The Nevis is 134m if that is too tame.

items.name: Milford Sound day cruise
items.description: Long drive through Fiordland to Mitre Peak and waterfalls straight off the cliffs.

items.name: Skyline Gondola and luge
items.description: Steepest cable car lift in the southern hemisphere, then a downhill luge track at the top.

items.name: Fergburger
items.description: The queue is real and the burger justifies it. Open until 5am.

items.name: Gibbston Valley wine tour
items.description: Central Otago Pinot Noir tasted in a cave cellar, twenty minutes from town.

items.name: Lake Wakatipu jet boat
items.description: Shotover canyon at 85km/h, inches from the rock walls, with 360-degree spins.
